planting.note: Plant divisions in fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this Sichuan/Chongqing species is slow to establish from its short, compact rhizome but forms a tidy, well-behaved clump rather than spreading aggressively.

directions: Plant divisions in fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, and once established this species tolerates the dry shade found under mature trees better than many perennials. Epimedium brachyrrhizum is a woodland species from the Chongqing region of China, named for its unusually short, compact rhizome, which gives it a clumping rather than running habit compared to more vigorously spreading epimediums. Large, elongated, spiny-margined leaflets emerge with a bronze-red flush in spring before maturing to leathery, semi-evergreen dark green foliage that provides structure through much of the year. In mid-spring, wiry stems carry loose sprays of pale yellow to creamy white flowers with slender spurs, held just above the foliage where they are easy to appreciate up close. Its restrained, non-invasive habit makes it well suited to smaller shaded borders and rock gardens where larger running epimediums would be unwelcome; comb out old foliage in late winter before the new flower spikes emerge.
